A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDC research work. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including v2's Appendices A–B. The supplied v1 ends with references and contains no bundled appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CDC clustering and calibration results on six image benchmarks, plus initialization, sample-selection and calibration-loss experiments in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original CDC benchmark results and reports additional failure-rejection evaluations and component ablations in Figure 3 and Tables 2, 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Both versions retain MoCo-v2 pretraining, prototype initialization with orthogonalization, dual heads, mini-cluster calibration targets, entropy regularization and confidence-aware pseudo-label selection. Algorithm 1 preserves the same parameter updates. v2's explicit stop-gradient discussion explains a restriction already present in v1's algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-20, STL-10, ImageNet-10, ImageNet-Dogs and Tiny-ImageNet, including STL-10's additional pretraining images. The new failure-rejection analysis examines existing CIFAR-20 predictions; it adds confidence-assessment metrics without introducing another dataset, population or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2's Tables 1 and 4 add raw-input K-means, TCL, TCC, DMICC, CoNR and DivClust as reported comparators. SeCu and SeCu-Size also gain STL-10 comparisons, and Figure 4 adds CC and SCAN training trajectories. Appendix B.1 identifies several added benchmark results as taken from cited papers rather than rerun.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design with AUROC, FPR95 and a metric named AURC in Section 4 but ARPC in Figure 3. New controlled experiments vary head configuration, gradient propagation, sample inclusion, MLP depth and entropy-loss weight. The retained CDC training budgets and dataset splits match; additional baseline-training disclosures do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds failure-separation analyses, single-head and combined-loss controls, stop-gradient ablation, all-versus-selected-sample training comparisons, and depth/entropy-weight sensitivity tests. It replaces the initialization-only training plots with comparisons against other methods. Conversely, v1's SCAN calibration-strength sweep and K-means-only initialization control disappear. Fixed-threshold results and calibration-loss reliability diagrams are retained.

E5.justification: v2's Figure 4 introduces shaded envelopes around training curves, absent from v1's corresponding plots. Neither its caption nor surrounding text explains whether these represent variation across runs, statistical uncertainty or another quantity. Neither PDF specifies seeds, repeated-run counts or interval estimation, leaving the statistical meaning of this visual change unresolved.

E6.justification: CDC's main benchmark scores remain unchanged, with NMI relocated to v2's Table 4. Numerous comparator, ablation and failure-rejection results are added, while some earlier ablation entries disappear. Existing numbers also change: ProPos CIFAR-20 ACC/NMI becomes 61.4/60.6 instead of 60.6/61.4, and initialization ECE becomes 5.2 instead of 45.6. Supervised CIFAR-20 ACC changes from 73.7 to 71.7 in the main table, although v2's Figure 6 retains 73.7.

T1.justification: v1 presents method equations without formal guarantees. v2 introduces Property 1 on prototype initialization, Theorem 1 on region-dependent confidence penalties, and Theorem 2 on calibration improvement, with proofs in Appendix A. These add substantial mathematical reasoning, including a binary Gaussian model and conditions governing the claimed ECE improvement.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and introduction newly claim theoretical guarantees for both calibration and initialization, substantially expanding the contributions beyond v1's empirical justification. The principal claims of a first calibrated deep clustering framework, approximately tenfold ECE improvement and strong clustering accuracy remain.

C2.justification: v2 develops a decision-boundary interpretation of reliable and unreliable regions, distinguishes low ECE from effective failure rejection, and explains gradient stopping and conflicting single-head losses. Section 5 newly states the known-cluster-count limitation, while Appendix A.4 excludes the underconfidence case from its guarantee. v1 contains only the earlier, less developed penalty and dual-head explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly documents GPU hardware, representation-learning augmentations, projector architecture, optimizers, schedules, supervised-baseline training and result provenance, plus a SPICE model-access link. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, v1's explicit CDC sub-batch sizes and zero weight decay are omitted, despite sub-batching remaining in Algorithm 1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting newer comparators, failure rejection, mixup-related calibration theory and training procedures. These broaden the supporting literature, but the related-work taxonomy and central positioning as the first calibrated deep clustering framework remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The method narrative is substantially reorganized: initialization precedes calibration and clustering, notation receives an opening treatment, and joint training/final prediction becomes a separate subsection. Experimental details and the algorithm move into appendices. The introduction and results discussion are extensively rewritten, and the conclusion gains an explicit limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to one, merges the head-architecture illustration into Figure 2, expands Figure 1, and splits the main results into ACC/ARI/ECE and appendix NMI tables. It reorganizes ablation tables, replaces training plots, and adds failure-rejection graphics, a calibration example and additional reliability diagrams.

improvement.justification: Additional controls, broader comparisons and detailed implementation information strengthen v2. However, its newly advertised theoretical guarantees have substantive proof gaps: Appendix A.1 drops the prototype-norm term without an equal-norm assumption, and A.4(ii) supplies an insufficient condition for its concluding inequality. Reporting reliability also worsens: Section 4.1 gives 40.6 as the CIFAR-20 calibration endpoint where Table 1 reports CDC-Cal ECE of 4.9. These benefits and material correctness problems leave the net quality change uncertain.
